It starts with a short, time-boxed documentation phase (design brief, content inventory, wireframes, tokens, motion spec, architecture) because no code is written until the big decisions have written answers. A deployed, themed, budgeted skeleton then proves hosting, CI, theming and reduced-motion handling before anything is built on top. Next comes a content-complete site with navigation, resume and copy-email, so the recruiter fast path works before any motion is layered on. The motion system and the signature project rail (reference 539: hover/lift on desktop, swipe and tap on touch, focused overlay) come after that. The rail is the first real use of the animation layer, and the phase ends with measured keep-or-drop decisions on react-spring and LazyMotion. Section treatments (experience cards, skills slider, education card, hero text effect) follow. Real-device hardening and the additive cutover into `aa-phan.github.io` come last, so the v1 iPod site stays live and rollback stays trivial until the new site has passed every gate.\n\n## Phases\n\n**Phase Numbering:**\n\n- Integer phases (1, 2, 3): Planned milestone work\n- Decimal phases (2.1, 2.2): Urgent insertions (marked with INSERTED)\n\nDecimal phases appear between their surrounding integers in numeric order.\n\n- [x] **Phase 1: Decisions and Documentation** - Time-boxed design, content, IA, tokens, motion and architecture docs that gate all code (completed 2026-10-09)\n- [x] **Phase 2: Deployed Themed Skeleton** - Vite/React/TS/Tailwind app live on the project URL with CI, JS budget, light/dark tokens and one motion-preference source (completed 2026-10-26)\n- [ ] **Phase 3: Content-Complete Site** - All six sections with real content, resume download, copy-email and navigation, passing the 10-second phone test\n- [ ] **Phase 4: Motion System and Signature Rail** - Shared motion rules plus the handled-object project rail with overlay, touch and keyboard paths\n- [ ] **Phase 5: Section Treatments** - Expandable experience cards, skills slider, education card and hero text effect\n- [ ] **Phase 6: Hardening and Cutover** - Lighthouse, real-device, keyboard/VoiceOver/axe gates, launch assets, and the additive cutover with a written rollback\n\n## Phase Details\n\n### Phase 1: Decisions and Documentation\n\n**Goal:** As a site owner, I want to have time-boxed design, content, motion and architecture docs, so that every major decision is settled before any code is written.\n**Mode:** mvp\n**Depends on**: Nothing (first phase)\n**Requirements**: DOC-01, DOC-02, DOC-03, DOC-04, DOC-05, DOC-06, CNT-03\n**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):\n\n  1. A content inventory lists every section and item to carry over (5 experience entries, 7 projects, education with GPA, public email, DJ Instagram link, resume), with the Symbotic metrics conflict and date formats resolved against `references/Aaron_Phan_Resume.pdf`, and each content gap marked as supplied, deferred or dropped.\n  3. Information architecture and wireframes exist at 375, 768 and 1280 px showing the recruiter fast path, plus the project rail and overlay in both a desktop (hover) form and a touch (swipe and tap) form.\n  4. A design tokens doc records the palette and type chosen via realtimecolors after exploring alternatives to the seed indigo, as light and dark sets, with a contrast matrix of text, UI and focus pairs in both themes that meets WCAG 2.2 AA on paper.\n  5. A motion spec lists each interaction with its owner library, touch equivalent and reduced-motion fallback, and an architecture doc, an ADR log (open decisions listed) and a deploy runbook draft exist.\n\n**Plans:** 7/7 plans complete\n\nPlans:\n**Wave 1**\n\n- [x] 01-01-PLAN.md — Tracer: Contact Me slice through inventory, wireframes, tokens and contrast checker; design brief; motion catalog seed (wave 1)\n\n**Wave 2** *(blocked on Wave 1 completion)*\n\n- [x] 01-02-PLAN.md — docs/architecture.md, ADR log, ADR-0001 doc split, ADR-0002 skeleton-gate skip, ignore references/ (wave 2)\n- [x] 01-03-PLAN.md — Content inventory reconciled against the resume, gap rulings checkpoint (wave 2)\n- [x] 01-04-PLAN.md — Three palette and type candidates, user pick, contrast matrix and tokens (wave 2)\n- [x] 01-05-PLAN.md — Motion spec: tokens, reduced motion, ownership matrix, 17 interactions (wave 2)\n\n**Wave 3** *(blocked on Wave 2 completion)*\n\n- [x] 01-06-PLAN.md — ADR-0003..0006 (Pages source, TS 6, SVG icons, dialog a11y) and deploy runbook (wave 3)\n\n**Wave 4** *(blocked on Wave 3 completion)*\n\n- [x] 01-07-PLAN.md — IA and wireframes at 375/768/1280, rail/overlay/nav states, cross-doc check (wave 4)\n\n**Cross-cutting constraints:**\n\n- No file under docs/ contains a phone number, a private planning path or a planning decision ID\n\n### Phase 2: Deployed Themed Skeleton\n\n**Goal:** As a visitor, I want to open the deployed project URL and see a fast, themed hero in light or dark, so that hosting, CI, theming and motion risks are retired before content is built.\n**Mode:** mvp\n**Depends on**: Phase 1\n**Requirements**: FND-01, FND-02, FND-03, FND-04, DSN-01, DSN-02, DSN-03, DSN-04, MOT-01, NAV-01\n**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):\n\n  1. No router, no global store, no data fetching.\n59\t\n60\t**Key Characteristics:**\n61\t- Build-time content: all copy lives in `src/content/*.ts`, checked against `src/content/schema.ts` with `satisfies`\n62\t- One page, one scroll-spy: `src/app/Page.tsx` renders every section in a fixed order\n63\t- Three small React contexts only: theme, motion preference, toast (plus optional active `nav-items.ts`\n87\t- Depends on: `@/anim` barrel, `src/lib/`, `src/hooks/`\n88\t- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx`, `src/sections/*`\n89\t\n90\t**UI components:**\n91\t- Purpose: Reusable controls\n92\t- layout, components, app providers\n103\t\n104\t**Content:**\n105\t- Purpose: Typed copy and data\n106\t- Location: `src/content/`\n107\t- Contains: `schema.ts`, `profile.ts`, `experience.ts`, `projects.ts`, `skills.ts`, `education.ts`, `contacts.ts`, `images.ts`, `index.ts`\n108\t- Depends on: `src/assets/images/` via `images.ts`\n109\t- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx` not-found page\n116\t\n117\t## Data Flow\n118\t\n119\t### Primary Request Path (page load)\n120\t\n121\t1. Browser loads `index.html`; an inline script in `<head>` reads localStorage and sets `data-theme` before first paint (`index.html`, `src/lib/theme.ts`)\n122\t2. Module entry `src/main.tsx` mounts `<App />` into `#root` in `StrictMode`\n123\t3. `src/app/App.tsx` renders `Providers` around `Page`\n124\t4. `src/app/Page.tsx` reads `siteContent` from `src/content/index.ts` and passes props to each section\n125\t5. Sections render JSX; wrappers in `src/anim/` apply motion or react-spring behaviour based on the motion preference\n126\t\n127\t### Theme Toggle Flow\n128\t\n129\t1. `src/components/ui/ThemeToggle.tsx` calls the hook in `src/hooks/useTheme.ts`\n130\t2. Hook updates `data-theme` on `<html>` and persists through `src/lib/theme.ts` (localStorage)\n131\t3. CSS tokens in `src/styles/tokens.css` re-resolve; no React re-render of content is needed\n132\t\n133\t### Scroll-Spy and Navigation Flow\n134\t\n135\t1. `src/app/Page.tsx` calls `useActiveSection(SECTION_IDS)` from `src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts`\n136\t2. An IntersectionObserver over section ids returns `activeId`; `lockTo` is set on user navigation\n137\t3. `activeId` feeds `SiteHeader` (desktop nav) and `PillNav` (phone pill), both in `src/layout/`\n138\t\n139\t### Project Detail Flow\n140\t\n141\t1. Click or tap on a project card in `src/sections/Projects/Projects.tsx` sets local state\n142\t2. `src/sections/Projects/ProjectDialog.tsx` opens with focus handling (native dialog, see `docs/adr/0009-native-dialog-for-project-details.md`)\n143\t\n144\t### Build-Time Flow\n145\t\n146\t```text\n147\tsrc/content/*.ts --(typed, satisfies)--> src/app/Page.tsx --props--> sections --props--> layout, ui\n148\tsrc/assets/*     --(vite-imagetools, hashed imports)--> image fields in content\n149\t```\n150\t\n151\t**State Management:**\n152\t- No global store. Contexts: theme (`src/hooks/useTheme.ts`), motion preference (`src/anim/MotionPreferenceProvider.tsx`), toast (`src/components/ui/Toast.tsx`), and optionally active section. All other state is local component state or props.\n153\t- Pointer-driven values are written to the DOM through react-spring without per-frame React renders.\n154\t\n155\t## Key Abstractions\n156\t\n157\t**Content schema:**\n158\t- Purpose: Single typed contract for all site data\n159\t- Examples: `src/content/schema.ts` (types `Profile`, `Project`, `ExperienceEntry`, `EducationEntry`, `SkillGroup`, `ContactLink`, `DateRange`, `ImageAsset`)\n160\t- Pattern: Data modules with `satisfies` against schema; ordering stored in data\n161\t\n162\t**Motion preference:**\n163\t- Purpose: One source for reduced-motion state, feeding motion, react-spring and CSS\n164\t- Examples: `src/anim/useMotionPreference.ts`, `src/anim/MotionPreferenceProvider.tsx`\n165\t- Pattern: Context provider; applies `MotionConfig` and `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })`\n166\t\n167\t**Animation wrappers:**\n168\t- Purpose: Semantic animated components so sections never call libraries directly\n169\t- Examples: `src/anim/declarative/ToastPresence.tsx`, `src/anim/declarative/NavIndicator.tsx`, `src/anim/declarative/PillMorph.tsx`, `src/anim/declarative/TextReveal.tsx`, `src/anim/physics/ThemeThumb.tsx`\n170\t- Pattern: Wrapper components that read motion preference, render an instant equivalent when reduced, and forward `className`\n171\t\n172\t**Design tokens:**\n173\t- Purpose: Five role colors per theme, all derived values computed from them\n174\t- Examples: `src/styles/tokens.css`, `src/anim/tokens.ts` (spring values mirrored to CSS)\n175\t- Pattern: CSS custom properties with `color-mix(in oklch, ...)`; Tailwind `@theme inline` maps utilities to variables\n176\t\n177\t**Lazy motion features:**\n178\t- Purpose: Keep the motion feature bundle out of the initial chunk\n179\t- Examples: `src/anim/features.ts` (`domMax`), `src/anim/MotionFeatures.tsx`\n180\t- Pattern: Dynamic chunk behind `LazyMotion`\n181\t\n182\t## Entry Points\n183\t\n184\t**Browser document (main):**\n185\t- Location: `index.html`\n186\t- Triggers: Page load of the site root\n187\t- Responsibilities: Meta and social tags, inline theme-init script, noscript fallback content, module script to `src/main.tsx`\n188\t\n189\t**Not-found document:**\n190\t- Location: `404.html`\n191\t- Triggers: GitHub Pages serves it for unknown paths\n192\t- Responsibilities: Static not-found page (second Vite input declared in `vite.config.ts`)\n193\t\n194\t**React root:**\n195\t- Location: `src/main.tsx`\n196\t- Triggers: Module script execution\n197\t- Responsibilities: Global CSS and font imports, `createRoot`, `StrictMode`\n198\t\n199\t**Build and dev:**\n200\t- Location: `vite.config.ts`\n201\t- Triggers: `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:e2e` (build first)\n202\t- Responsibilities: `base` from `VITE_BASE`, React and Tailwind plugins, imagetools, `@` alias, two HTML inputs\n203\t\n204\t**Quality gates:**\n205\t- Location: `package.json` `verify` script, `scripts/*.mjs`\n206\t- Triggers: `npm run verify`, CI workflows\n207\t- Responsibilities: Typecheck, lint, format, tests, color/contrast/case checks, build, JS budget, phone and image checks\n208\t\n209\t## Architectural Constraints\n210\t\n211\t- **Threading:** Single-threaded browser event loop. No workers, no server runtime.\n212\t- **Global state:** Module-level content objects in `src/content/index.ts` (`siteContent`) are read-only data. The theme value is mirrored on the `<html>` `data-theme` attribute and in localStorage. Global react-spring configuration is set via `Globals.assign` in the motion preference provider.\n213\t- **Circular imports:** None detected in the import graph described by the layer rules.\n214\t- **Import boundaries:** Only `src/anim/` and `src/components/motion-primitives/` may import `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web`. Only `src/app/Page.tsx` may import `src/content/`. Enforced by `.oxlintrc.json` `no-restricted-imports`.\n215\t- **Path alias:** `@/` resolves to `src/` (`vite.config.ts`, and `tsconfig` paths). Imports must match file-name case (`scripts/check-path-case.mjs`).\n216\t\n217\t## Anti-Patterns\n218\t\n219\t### Importing an animation library outside the anim layer\n220\t\n221\t**What happens:** A section or layout file imports `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web` directly.\n222\t**Why it's wrong:** Breaks the single-animation-API seam and reduced-motion handling, and fails `oxlint` in CI.\n223\t**Do this instead:** Add or reuse a wrapper in `src/anim/declarative/` or `src/anim/physics/` and export it from `src/anim/index.ts` (see `docs/architecture.md`, Import rules).\n224\t\n225\t### Importing content data outside Page.tsx\n226\t\n227\t**What happens:** A section component imports from `src/content/` (for example `src/content/projects.ts`) to read data directly.\n228\t**Why it's wrong:** Sections become coupled to data and cannot be rendered from props in tests or fixtures.\n229\t**Do this instead:** Pass data down from `src/app/Page.tsx` as props, typed with the content types re-exported from `src/content/index.ts`.\n230\t\n231\t### Hiding content until JavaScript runs\n232\t\n233\t**What happens:** An animation wrapper sets content to `opacity: 0` or `display: none` in its initial CSS state.\n234\t**Why it's wrong:** The hero must be visible with JavaScript off, and the smoke tests check this (`tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts`).\n235\t**Do this instead:** Apply hidden initial states client-side inside the wrapper, and rely on the `noscript` rule in `src/styles/base.css`.\n236\t\n237\t## Error Handling\n238\t\n239\t**Strategy:** Defensive fallbacks at the edge (clipboard, storage) rather than error boundaries. No error boundary component was detected under `src/`.\n240\t\n241\t**Patterns:**\n242\t- Clipboard access is guarded with `navigator.clipboard?.writeText` in `src/lib/copy.ts`\n243\t- localStorage access is wrapped in `src/lib/theme.ts`\n244\t- Build-time gates fail the build with explicit messages (`scripts/check-no-phone.mjs`, `scripts/check-images.mjs`)\n245\t\n246\t## Cross-Cutting Concerns\n247\t\n248\t**Logging:** None at runtime. Build scripts print to console.\n249\t**Validation:** Compile-time via `satisfies` and TypeScript; content invariants (unique ids, resolvable related ids, alt text, https links, date order) tested in `tests/unit/content.test.ts`.\n250\t**Authentication:** Not applicable.\n251\t**Accessibility:** Skip link (`src/layout/SkipLink.tsx`), focus ring and reduced-motion guard in `src/styles/base.css`, contrast checks (`scripts/check-contrast.mjs`).\n252\t\n253\t---\n254\t\n255\t*Architecture analysis: Overview\n\n```text\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                  Entry: `index.html` → `src/main.tsx`        │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│   `src/app/App.tsx` → `Providers` → `Page`                   │\n│   (Page.tsx is the only file that imports content data)      │\n└────────┬───────────────────────┬────────────────────┬────────┘\n         │                       │                    │\n         ▼                       ▼                    ▼\n┌────────────────┐   ┌──────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐\n│ `src/sections/`│   │ `src/layout/`        │  │ `src/components/ │\n│ Hero, About,   │   │ SiteHeader, PillNav, │  │ ui/`         │\n        ▼                       ▼                       ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  `src/anim/` (only importer of motion/react, react-spring)   │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  `src/hooks/`, `src/lib/`, `src/styles/` (CSS tokens)        │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│  `src/content/` (typed data), `src/assets/` (images, fonts)  │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n## Component Responsibilities\n\n| Component | Responsibility | File |\n|-----------|----------------|------|\n| Bootstrap | Mounts React root inside `StrictMode`, imports global CSS and font | `src/main.tsx` |\n| App shell | Composes providers and page | `src/app/App.tsx` |\n| Providers | Wraps tree in motion preference, lazy motion features, toast context | `src/app/Providers.tsx` |\n| Page | Assembles siteContent into sections; owns scroll-spy and nav wiring | `src/app/Page.tsx` |\n| Content model | Typed content data and schema | `src/content/schema.ts`, `src/content/index.ts` |\n| Sections | Presentational section components (props in, JSX out) | `src/sections/*/` |\n| Layout | Header, pill navigation, footer, container, skip link | `src/layout/*.tsx` |\n| Animation layer | Only place that imports `motion/react` and `@react-spring/web` | `src/anim/index.ts` |\n| Vendored primitives | Patched third-party motion components | `src/components/motion-primitives/text-effect.tsx` |\n| UI primitives | CTA link, theme toggle, toast, inline SVG icons | `src/components/ui/` |\n| Theme logic | Read/write theme in localStorage and `data-theme` attribute | `src/lib/theme.ts`, `src/hooks/useTheme.ts` |\n| Scroll-spy | IntersectionObserver driving active nav section | `src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts` |\n| Design tokens | Five role colors per theme, derived via `color-mix` | `src/styles/tokens.css` |\n\n## Pattern Overview\n\n**Overall:** Static single-page React app with a typed-content layer, layered component tree and CSS-variable theming. No router, no global store, no data fetching.\n\n**Key Characteristics:**\n- Build-time content: all copy lives in `src/content/*.ts`, checked against `src/content/schema.ts` with `satisfies`\n- One page, one scroll-spy: `src/app/Page.tsx` renders every section in a fixed order\n- Three small React contexts only: theme, motion preference, toast (plus optional active section); everything else is props\n- Layered import rules enforced by lint (see `.oxlintrc.json`), documented in `docs/architecture.md`\n- Client-side only at runtime; no network calls beyond same-origin assets\n\n## Layers\n\n**App (composition root):**\n- Purpose: Mount the app and wire content into sections\n- Location: `src/app/`\n- Contains: `App.tsx`, `Providers.tsx`, `Page.tsx`\n- Depends on: `src/content/`, `src/sections/`, `src/layout/`, `src/anim/`, `src/components/ui/Toast`, `src/hooks/useActiveSection`\n- Used by: `src/main.tsx`\n\n**Sections:**\n- Purpose: Render one portfolio section each from props\n- Location: `src/sections/Hero/`, `src/sections/About/`, `src/sections/Experience/`, `src/sections/Projects/`, `src/sections/Skills/`, `src/sections/Education/`, `src/sections/Contact/`\n- Contains: Section components and, for Projects, `ProjectDialog.tsx`, `Sleeve.tsx`, `project-types.ts`\n- Depends on: `src/layout/`, `src/components/ui/`, the `@/anim` barrel, content types (not data)\n- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx`\n\n**Layout:**\n- Purpose: Page chrome and shared structural wrappers\n- Location: `src/layout/`\n- Contains: `Container.tsx`, `Section.tsx`, `SiteHeader.tsx`, `PillNav.tsx`, `Footer.tsx`, `SkipLink.tsx`, `Wordmark.tsx`, `nav-items.ts`\n- Depends on: `@/anim` barrel, `src/lib/`, `src/hooks/`\n- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx`, `src/sections/*`\n\n**UI components:**\n- Purpose: Reusable controls\n- Location: `src/components/ui/`\n- Contains: `CtaLink.tsx`, `ThemeToggle.tsx`, `Toast.tsx`, `useToast.ts`, `useCopyEmail.ts`, `icons/`\n- Depends on: `src/lib/`, `src/hooks/`, `@/anim` barrel\n- Used by: sections, layout, app\n\n**Animation layer:**\n- Purpose: Single internal API over motion and react-spring\n- Location: `src/anim/`\n- Contains: `index.ts` (barrel), `MotionPreferenceProvider.tsx`, `useMotionPreference.ts`, `MotionFeatures.tsx`, `features.ts` (lazy `domMax` chunk), `tokens.ts` (springs and durations), `declarative/` (motion-owned wrappers), `physics/` (react-spring wrappers)\n- Depends on: `motion/react`, `@react-spring/web`, `src/components/motion-primitives/`, token mirror in `src/styles/`\n- Used by: sections, layout, components, app providers\n\n**Content:**\n- Purpose: Typed copy and data\n- Location: `src/content/`\n- Contains: `schema.ts`, `profile.ts`, `experience.ts`, `projects.ts`, `skills.ts`, `education.ts`, `contacts.ts`, `images.ts`, `index.ts`\n- Depends on: `src/assets/images/` via `images.ts`\n- Used by: `src/app/Page.tsx` only\n\n**Styling:**\n- Purpose: Design tokens and global CSS\n- Location: `src/styles/`\n- Contains: `index.css` (Tailwind import, custom dark variant, `@theme inline`), `tokens.css` (role and derived tokens, light and dark blocks), `base.css`, `interactions.css`, `not-found.css`\n- Used by: `src/main.tsx` imports `src/styles/index.css`; `404.html` for the not-found page\n\n## Data Flow\n\n### Primary Request Path (page load)\n\n1. Browser loads `index.html`; an inline script in `<head>` reads localStorage and sets `data-theme` before first paint (`index.html`, `src/lib/theme.ts`)\n2. Module entry `src/main.tsx` mounts `<App />` into `#root` in `StrictMode`\n3. `src/app/App.tsx` renders `Providers` around `Page`\n4. `src/app/Page.tsx` reads `siteContent` from `src/content/index.ts` and passes props to each section\n5. Sections render JSX; wrappers in `src/anim/` apply motion or react-spring behaviour based on the motion preference\n\n### Theme Toggle Flow\n\n1. `src/components/ui/ThemeToggle.tsx` calls the hook in `src/hooks/useTheme.ts`\n2. Hook updates `data-theme` on `<html>` and persists through `src/lib/theme.ts` (localStorage)\n3. CSS tokens in `src/styles/tokens.css` re-resolve; no React re-render of content is needed\n\n### Scroll-Spy and Navigation Flow\n\n1. `src/app/Page.tsx` calls `useActiveSection(SECTION_IDS)` from `src/hooks/useActiveSection.ts`\n2. An IntersectionObserver over section ids returns `activeId`; `lockTo` is set on user navigation\n3. `activeId` feeds `SiteHeader` (desktop nav) and `PillNav` (phone pill), both in `src/layout/`\n\n### Project Detail Flow\n\n1. Click or tap on a project card in `src/sections/Projects/Projects.tsx` sets local state\n2. `src/sections/Projects/ProjectDialog.tsx` opens with focus handling (native dialog, see `docs/adr/0009-native-dialog-for-project-details.md`)\n\n### Build-Time Flow\n\n```text\nsrc/content/*.ts --(typed, satisfies)--> src/app/Page.tsx --props--> sections --props--> layout, ui\nsrc/assets/*     --(vite-imagetools, hashed imports)--> image fields in content\n```\n\n**State Management:**\n- No global store. Contexts: theme (`src/hooks/useTheme.ts`), motion preference (`src/anim/MotionPreferenceProvider.tsx`), toast (`src/components/ui/Toast.tsx`), and optionally active section. All other state is local component state or props.\n- Pointer-driven values are written to the DOM through react-spring without per-frame React renders.\n\n## Key Abstractions\n\n**Content schema:**\n- Purpose: Single typed contract for all site data\n- Examples: `src/content/schema.ts` (types `Profile`, `Project`, `ExperienceEntry`, `EducationEntry`, `SkillGroup`, `ContactLink`, `DateRange`, `ImageAsset`)\n- Pattern: Data modules with `satisfies` against schema; ordering stored in data\n\n**Motion preference:**\n- Purpose: One source for reduced-motion state, feeding motion, react-spring and CSS\n- Examples: `src/anim/useMotionPreference.ts`, `src/anim/MotionPreferenceProvider.tsx`\n- Pattern: Context provider; applies `MotionConfig` and `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })`\n\n**Animation wrappers:**\n- Purpose: Semantic animated components so sections never call libraries directly\n- Examples: `src/anim/declarative/ToastPresence.tsx`, `src/anim/declarative/NavIndicator.tsx`, `src/anim/declarative/PillMorph.tsx`, `src/anim/declarative/TextReveal.tsx`, `src/anim/physics/ThemeThumb.tsx`\n- Pattern: Wrapper components that read motion preference, render an instant equivalent when reduced, and forward `className`\n\n**Design tokens:**\n- Purpose: Five role colors per theme, all derived values computed from them\n- Examples: `src/styles/tokens.css`, `src/anim/tokens.ts` (spring values mirrored to CSS)\n- Pattern: CSS custom properties with `color-mix(in oklch, ...)`; Tailwind `@theme inline` maps utilities to variables\n\n**Lazy motion features:**\n- Purpose: Keep the motion feature bundle out of the initial chunk\n- Examples: `src/anim/features.ts` (`domMax`), `src/anim/MotionFeatures.tsx`\n- Pattern: Dynamic chunk behind `LazyMotion`\n\n## Entry Points\n\n**Browser document (main):**\n- Location: `index.html`\n- Triggers: Page load of the site root\n- Responsibilities: Meta and social tags, inline theme-init script, noscript fallback content, module script to `src/main.tsx`\n\n**Not-found document:**\n- Location: `404.html`\n- Triggers: GitHub Pages serves it for unknown paths\n- Responsibilities: Static not-found page (second Vite input declared in `vite.config.ts`)\n\n**React root:**\n- Location: `src/main.tsx`\n- Triggers: Module script execution\n- Responsibilities: Global CSS and font imports, `createRoot`, `StrictMode`\n\n**Build and dev:**\n- Location: `vite.config.ts`\n- Triggers: `npm run dev`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:e2e` (build first)\n- Responsibilities: `base` from `VITE_BASE`, React and Tailwind plugins, imagetools, `@` alias, two HTML inputs\n\n**Quality gates:**\n- Location: `package.json` `verify` script, `scripts/*.mjs`\n- Triggers: `npm run verify`, CI workflows\n- Responsibilities: Typecheck, lint, format, tests, color/contrast/case checks, build, JS budget, phone and image checks\n\n## Architectural Constraints\n\n- **Threading:** Single-threaded browser event loop. No workers, no server runtime.\n- **Global state:** Module-level content objects in `src/content/index.ts` (`siteContent`) are read-only data. The theme value is mirrored on the `<html>` `data-theme` attribute and in localStorage. Global react-spring configuration is set via `Globals.assign` in the motion preference provider.\n- **Circular imports:** None detected in the import graph described by the layer rules.\n- **Import boundaries:** Only `src/anim/` and `src/components/motion-primitives/` may import `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web`. Only `src/app/Page.tsx` may import `src/content/`. Enforced by `.oxlintrc.json` `no-restricted-imports`.\n- **Path alias:** `@/` resolves to `src/` (`vite.config.ts`, and `tsconfig` paths). Imports must match file-name case (`scripts/check-path-case.mjs`).\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n### Importing an animation library outside the anim layer\n\n**What happens:** A section or layout file imports `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web` directly.\n**Why it's wrong:** Breaks the single-animation-API seam and reduced-motion handling, and fails `oxlint` in CI.\n**Do this instead:** Add or reuse a wrapper in `src/anim/declarative/` or `src/anim/physics/` and export it from `src/anim/index.ts` (see `docs/architecture.md`, Import rules).\n\n### Importing content data outside Page.tsx\n\n**What happens:** A section component imports from `src/content/` (for example `src/content/projects.ts`) to read data directly.\n**Why it's wrong:** Sections become coupled to data and cannot be rendered from props in tests or fixtures.\n**Do this instead:** Pass data down from `src/app/Page.tsx` as props, typed with the content types re-exported from `src/content/index.ts`.\n\n### Hiding content until JavaScript runs\n\n**What happens:** An animation wrapper sets content to `opacity: 0` or `display: none` in its initial CSS state.\n**Why it's wrong:** The hero must be visible with JavaScript off, and the smoke tests check this (`tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts`).\n**Do this instead:** Apply hidden initial states client-side inside the wrapper, and rely on the `noscript` rule in `src/styles/base.css`.\n\n## Error Handling\n\n**Strategy:** Defensive fallbacks at the edge (clipboard, storage) rather than error boundaries. No error boundary component was detected under `src/`.\n\n**Patterns:**\n- Clipboard access is guarded with `navigator.clipboard?.writeText` in `src/lib/copy.ts`\n- localStorage access is wrapped in `src/lib/theme.ts`\n- Build-time gates fail the build with explicit messages (`scripts/check-no-phone.mjs`, `scripts/check-images.mjs`)\n\n## Cross-Cutting Concerns\n\n**Logging:** None at runtime. Build scripts print to console.\n**Validation:** Compile-time via `satisfies` and TypeScript; content invariants (unique ids, resolvable related ids, alt text, https links, date order) tested in `tests/unit/content.test.ts`.\n**Authentication:** Not applicable.\n**Accessibility:** Skip link (`src/layout/SkipLink.tsx`), focus ring and reduced-motion guard in `src/styles/base.css`, contrast checks (`scripts/check-contrast.mjs`).\n\n---\n\n*Architecture analysis: 2026-11-19*\n","numLines":256,"startLine":1,"totalLines":256}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_013nmKe1syMReAAPsjz8YsTN","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

(`useTheme.ts`, `useActiveSection.ts`)\n- Non-component modules: kebab-case or lowercase (`nav-items.ts`, `project-types.ts`, `copy.ts`)\n- Content modules: lowercase noun per section `tests/e2e/`\n- Section folders: PascalCase matching the component (`src/sections/Hero/Hero.tsx`)\n\n**Directories:**\n- Source folders: lowercase (`anim`, `app`, `layout`, `lib`)\n- Section and icon folders: PascalCase where they hold one component family (`sections/Hero/`, `components/ui/icons/`)\n\n**Imports:**\n- Use the `@/` alias for anything under `src/` (for example `@/anim`, `@/layout/SiteHeader`)\n- Animation imports go through the `@/anim` barrel only\n- Import paths must match on-disk file-name case (checked by `scripts/check-path-case.mjs`)\n\n## Where to Add New Code\n\n**New Section:**\n- Component: `src/sections/<Name>/<Name>.tsx` (props in, JSX out)\n- Data: add a module under `src/content/` and register it in `src/content/index.ts` and `src/content/schema.ts`\n- Wire-up: pass the data from `src/app/Page.tsx` and add the id to `src/layout/nav-items.ts`\n- Tests: `tests/unit/` for logic, `tests/e2e/` for user flows\n\n**New Animated Behaviour:**\n- Wrapper: `src/anim/declarative/` (mount, presence, layout, scroll-linked, text) or `src/anim/physics/` (velocity, pointer-driven)\n- Export: add to `src/anim/index.ts`\n- Never import `motion/react` or `@react-spring/web` from sections, layout or components\n\n**New UI Component:**\n- Implementation: `src/components/ui/<Name>.tsx`\n- Icons: `src/components/ui/icons/<Name>Icon.tsx` (inline SVG, no icon package)\n\n**New Hook:**\n- Shared: `src/hooks/use<Name>.ts`\n\n**New Utility or Helper:**\n- Framework-agnostic: `src/lib/<name>.ts`\n- Class composition: extend `src/lib/utils.ts`\n\n**New Image:**\n- Source: `src/assets/images/<name>.<ext>`, registered in `src/content/images.ts`, imported as a module. No package.json, no npm install. It is a verification tool for the tokens doc, not application code (Phase 2 may port its logic into a token-contrast test). Implement: hex parsing; OKLCH to OKLab to linear sRGB using Ottosson's published matrices; a gamut check (each linear channel within -0.0001..1.0001, otherwise the row FAILs as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because browser gamut mapping would change the rendered color); WCAG 2.x relative luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on linear channels); contrast (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05), compared UNROUNDED against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to 2 decimals. Implement CSS color-mix(in oklch) semantics for derived tokens: mix(--a P%, --b) interpolates L and C linearly with weight P/100 on --a, hue along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color (C below 0.0001) adopts the other color's hue. Argument flags may appear before or after the doc path. Modes:\n126\t- --selftest: runs at least 9 checks and prints SELFTEST PASS n/n with exit 0, or one SELFTEST FAIL line per failed check with exit 1. Required checks: hex pairs 050315/fbfbfe = 19.73, 2f27ce/fbfbfe = 8.83, 2f27ce/050315 = 2.23, 433bff/050315 = 3.21, 7b75ff/050315 = 5.66, dedcff/fbfbfe = 1.29 (each within 0.01; values independently verified during planning); oklch(1 0 0) vs oklch(0 0 0) = 21.00; hex 2f27ce round-trips through OKLCH back to 2f27ce; a 50% mix of oklch(1 0 0) and oklch(0 0 0) has L = 0.5.\n127\t- --convert VALUE: given a hex prints oklch(L C H) (L as 0-1 decimal, 4 decimals), given oklch(...) prints hex. Used to author tokens and realtimecolors links.\n128\t- default, DOC [--require-chosen]: parse fenced blocks from DOC. Info string \"palette X\" (X = one uppercase letter) holds role lines \"THEME TOKEN oklch(L C H)\" (THEME is light or dark) and optional derived-override lines. Info string \"derived\" holds lines \"THEME TOKEN mix(TOKEN_A P%, TOKEN_B)\". constant), references/Aaron_Phan_Resume.pdf (via the redacting pipe below only)</read_first>\n  <action>\nAll four files live in the phase directory per D-01; wireframes are ASCII/markdown per D-02. This task builds one section through every planning-doc layer; other sections are added by plans 01-03, 01-04, 01-05 and 01-07 into the same files.\n\n(1) contrast-check.mjs — a Node ESM script using only node: built-ins (fs, path, process). No package.json, no npm install. It is a verification tool for the tokens doc, not application code (Phase 2 may port its logic into a token-contrast test). Implement: hex parsing; OKLCH to OKLab to linear sRGB using Ottosson's published matrices; a gamut check (each linear channel within -0.0001..1.0001, otherwise the row FAILs as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because browser gamut mapping would change the rendered color); WCAG 2.x relative luminance (0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B on linear channels); contrast (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05), compared UNROUNDED against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to 2 decimals. Implement CSS color-mix(in oklch) semantics for derived tokens: mix(--a P%, --b) interpolates L and C linearly with weight P/100 on --a, hue along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color (C below 0.0001) adopts the other color's hue. Argument flags may appear before or after the doc path. Modes:\n- --selftest: runs at least 9 checks and prints SELFTEST PASS n/n with exit 0, or one SELFTEST FAIL line per failed check with exit 1. Required checks: hex pairs 050315/fbfbfe = 19.73, 2f27ce/fbfbfe = 8.83, 2f27ce/050315 = 2.23, 433bff/050315 = 3.21, 7b75ff/050315 = 5.66, dedcff/fbfbfe = 1.29 (each within 0.01; values independently verified during planning); oklch(1 0 0) vs oklch(0 0 0) = 21.00; hex 2f27ce round-trips through OKLCH back to 2f27ce; a 50% mix of oklch(1 0 0) and oklch(0 0 0) has L = 0.5.\n- --convert VALUE: given a hex prints oklch(L C H) (L as 0-1 decimal, 4 decimals), given oklch(...) prints hex. Used to author tokens and realtimecolors links.\n- default, DOC [--require-chosen]: parse fenced blocks from DOC. Info string \"palette X\" (X = one uppercase letter) holds role lines \"THEME TOKEN oklch(L C H)\" (THEME is light or dark) and optional derived-override lines. Info string \"derived\" holds lines \"THEME TOKEN mix(TOKEN_A P%, TOKEN_B)\". Info string \"pairs\" holds lines \"FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY...\" where CATEGORY is text (min 4.5), large (3.0), ui (3.0) or focus (3.0). Enforce per D-06: every palette defines exactly the 5 roles --text, --background, --primary, --secondary, --accent for both light and dark; a derived token given a literal color is an error (derived tokens are mix() only); every pair token resolves. First print one line per resolved token, \"TOKEN PALETTE THEME NAME oklch(L C H) #rrggbb\" (roles and derived tokens alike), then print one row per palette x theme x pair: \"PALETTE THEME FG on BG CATEGORY RATIO min THRESHOLD PASS|FAIL USED-BY\". Final line: \"RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M\" with exit 0, or \"RESULT: FAIL failures=K\" with exit 1. Exit 2 with an \"ERROR:\" line when no palette block or no pairs line is found, or any block fails to parse. With --require-chosen the doc must contain a line \"Chosen palette: X\" naming an existing palette block (print \"CHOSEN X\"), else exit 1.\n\n(2) 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md — first line after the title: \"Status: Draft\". One format is used for every date on the site and in this file.\n\n1. Month names are written in full: January, February, and so on. No abbreviations, no numeric months.\n2. A single date is `Month YYYY`, for example `July 2026`.\n3. A range is `Month YYYY – Month YYYY`: an en dash (U+2013) with one space on each side, and the year written on both sides, for example `May 2025 – August 2025`.\n4. Resume abbreviations are expanded. The resume's `Aug. 2022` becomes `August 2022`.\n5. Legacy hyphen ranges and short months are normalized. The legacy `June 2023 - Aug 2023` becomes `June 2023 – August 2023`.\n6. Academic-term labels (Spring 2024, Fall 2023, Summer 2022) are converted to month ranges per the G-08 ruling. The original label is kept in the item's Legacy-site value.\n7. This policy is applied to every date in the file. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01JPhkZmZnDuQ4Gw2cSTxhTJ","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Design Brief (DOC-01)\n2\t\n3\tStatus: Accepted\n4\t\n5\tThis brief sets the intent every later doc and phase is checked against. When a design or content choice is unclear, this file decides.\n6\t\n7\t## Purpose\n8\t\n9\tA remake of Aaron Phan's personal portfolio, currently the click-wheel iPod site, as a playful, tactile React site with a strong visual identity. The iPod concept is dropped entirely; the new site has its own identity. The content stays the same (same six sections, existing copy and images, updated from the current resume) and the presentation is new.\n10\t\n11\t## Audience\n12\t\n13\tRecruiters and hiring managers, and the design-engineering community, served equally. Recruiters need name, role, experience, projects, resume and contact fast. The design-engineering audience looks for craft in how the page feels. The site has to satisfy both without making either wait.\n14\t\n15\t## Core value\n16\t\n17\tThe site must feel crafted and memorable (tactile, physics-based motion and strong visual identity) while key info stays instantly accessible, on mobile as much as desktop.\n18\t\n19\t## Personality\n20\t\n21\tPlayful, tactile, crafted, plus four more.\n22\t\n23\t- **Playful:** small surprises reward curiosity (a role line that cycles, a copy-email toast that eases in) without blocking anything.\n24\t- **Tactile:** buttons and cards press and squish, the project rail is something you handle, and motion carries weight and settles like a physical object.\n25\t- **Crafted:** consistent spacing, type and motion tokens; nothing looks defaulted; details such as focus rings and reduced-motion states are designed, not patched.\n26\t- **Warm:** soft shapes, large friendly type and gentle color bands, taken from the tone reference.\n27\t- **Confident:** short, plain copy that states what Aaron does and has built, with no filler.\n28\t- **Fast:** pages load quickly on a phone and every interaction responds immediately.\n29\t- **Inclusive:** keyboard, screen reader and reduced-motion users get the same content and the same personality in a calmer form.\n30\t\n31\t## Anti-goals\n32\t\n33\t- Scroll-jacking: the page scrolls natively on touch and never traps the wheel.\n34\t- A preloader or intro animation that blocks content.\n35\t- Hover-only content: everything reachable by hover is also reachable by tap and keyboard.\n36\t- A site-wide custom cursor.\n37\t- 3D or WebGL.\n38\t- Skill percentage bars.\n39\t- Effects stacked on every card: one spatial idea, used where it earns its place.\n40\t- The phone number anywhere.\n41\t\n42\t## The 10-second test\n43\t\n44\tA first-time visitor on a phone can find name, role, experience, projects, resume and contact within 10 seconds.\n45\t\n46\t| Item | Where it lives | How it is reached |\n47\t|------|----------------|-------------------|\n48\t| Name | {#hero} | Visible on first paint with no scrolling |\n49\t| Role | {#hero} | The role line directly under the name |\n50\t| Experience | {#experience} | Bottom pill nav: the Experience segment, one tap |\n51\t| Projects | {#projects} | Bottom pill nav: the Projects segment, one tap |\n52\t| Resume | {#hero} | The hero Resume CTA, one tap |\n53\t| Contact | {#contact} | Hero Contact CTA, one tap (also in the pill Menu panel) |\n54\t\n55\tPass rule: all six found in 10 seconds or less, timed on a real phone with motion enabled.\n56\t\n57\t## References\n58\t\n59\tSource clips are in `references/` (private, not in the public repo). Notes come from still frames, so timing and physics are inferred; the feel is verified with the user during the interaction work.\n60\t\n61\t### 539 — Handled project rail (signature)\n62\t\n63\tThe signature interaction: an object you handle. On hover a project lifts out and enlarges while its neighbors shift aside; a click opens a focused detail view with the rail blurred behind it, prev and next controls, an index and a close control. On touch the visitor swipes the rail and taps to open.\n64\t\n65\t- Borrow: the lift, the neighbors making room, the focused detail with a blurred backdrop, prev/next with an index, and a clear close control.\n66\t- Do not borrow: hover as the only way in (touch uses swipe and tap), the garment-and-hanger metaphor, the newsletter ticker, and the corner-only About/Contact placement.\n67\t\n68\t### 445 — Morphing pill nav (mobile)\n69\t\n70\tA bottom pill expands in place into frosted panels, then collapses. One element morphs between states, which is the strongest mobile pattern in the set.\n71\t\n72\t- Borrow: the single pill that expands and collapses in place, the frosted panel surface, and the one-element-morphs idea.\n73\t- Do not borrow: the audiobook-specific panels (search, settings) and the phone-mockup framing.\n74\t\n75\t### 355 — Tone\n76\t\n77\tA soft marketing site with a pastel hero, cream and navy alternating bands, a card carousel, an accordion list and an oversized wordmark footer. It is the tone reference, not the signature.\n78\t\n79\t- Borrow: softness, large type, and alternating background bands between sections.\n80\t- Do not borrow: the cursor-reactive text distortion (hover-only and a site-wide cursor effect), the illustration set, and the cloud-textured wordmark.\n81\t\n82\t### godly.design — Mood board\n83\t\n84\tCurated posts of interface interaction clips. When a design or content choice is unclear, this file decides.\n\n## Purpose\n\nA remake of Aaron Phan's personal portfolio, currently the click-wheel iPod site, as a playful, tactile React site with a strong visual identity. The iPod concept is dropped entirely; the new site has its own identity. The content stays the same (same six sections, existing copy and images, updated from the current resume) and the presentation is new.\n\n## Audience\n\nRecruiters and hiring managers, and the design-engineering community, served equally. Recruiters need name, role, experience, projects, resume and contact fast. The design-engineering audience looks for craft in how the page feels. The site has to satisfy both without making either wait.\n\n## Core value\n\nThe site must feel crafted and memorable (tactile, physics-based motion and strong visual identity) while key info stays instantly accessible, on mobile as much as desktop.\n\n## Personality\n\nPlayful, tactile, crafted, plus four more.\n\n- **Playful:** small surprises reward curiosity (a role line that cycles, a copy-email toast that eases in) without blocking anything.\n- **Tactile:** buttons and cards press and squish, the project rail is something you handle, and motion carries weight and settles like a physical object.\n- **Crafted:** consistent spacing, type and motion tokens; nothing looks defaulted; details such as focus rings and reduced-motion states are designed, not patched.\n- **Warm:** soft shapes, large friendly type and gentle color bands, taken from the tone reference.\n- **Confident:** short, plain copy that states what Aaron does and has built, with no filler.\n- **Fast:** pages load quickly on a phone and every interaction responds immediately.\n- **Inclusive:** keyboard, screen reader and reduced-motion users get the same content and the same personality in a calmer form.\n\n## Anti-goals\n\n- Scroll-jacking: the page scrolls natively on touch and never traps the wheel.\n- A preloader or intro animation that blocks content.\n- Hover-only content: everything reachable by hover is also reachable by tap and keyboard.\n- A site-wide custom cursor.\n- 3D or WebGL.\n- Skill percentage bars.\n- Effects stacked on every card: one spatial idea, used where it earns its place.\n- The phone number anywhere.\n\n## The 10-second test\n\nA first-time visitor on a phone can find name, role, experience, projects, resume and contact within 10 seconds.\n\n| Item | Where it lives | How it is reached |\n|------|----------------|-------------------|\n| Name | {#hero} | Visible on first paint with no scrolling |\n| Role | {#hero} | The role line directly under the name |\n| Experience | {#experience} | Bottom pill nav: the Experience segment, one tap |\n| Projects | {#projects} | Bottom pill nav: the Projects segment, one tap |\n| Resume | {#hero} | The hero Resume CTA, one tap |\n| Contact | {#contact} | Hero Contact CTA, one tap (also in the pill Menu panel) |\n\nPass rule: all six found in 10 seconds or less, timed on a real phone with motion enabled.\n\n## References\n\nSource clips are in `references/` (private, not in the public repo). Notes come from still frames, so timing and physics are inferred; the feel is verified with the user during the interaction work.\n\n### 539 — Handled project rail (signature)\n\nThe signature interaction: an object you handle. On hover a project lifts out and enlarges while its neighbors shift aside; a click opens a focused detail view with the rail blurred behind it, prev and next controls, an index and a close control. On touch the visitor swipes the rail and taps to open.\n\n- Borrow: the lift, the neighbors making room, the focused detail with a blurred backdrop, prev/next with an index, and a clear close control.\n- Do not borrow: hover as the only way in (touch uses swipe and tap), the garment-and-hanger metaphor, the newsletter ticker, and the corner-only About/Contact placement.\n\n### 445 — Morphing pill nav (mobile)\n\nA bottom pill expands in place into frosted panels, then collapses. One element morphs between states, which is the strongest mobile pattern in the set.\n\n- Borrow: the single pill that expands and collapses in place, the frosted panel surface, and the one-element-morphs idea.\n- Do not borrow: the audiobook-specific panels (search, settings) and the phone-mockup framing.\n\n### 355 — Tone\n\nA soft marketing site with a pastel hero, cream and navy alternating bands, a card carousel, an accordion list and an oversized wordmark footer. It is the tone reference, not the signature.\n\n- Borrow: softness, large type, and alternating background bands between sections.\n- Do not borrow: the cursor-reactive text distortion (hover-only and a site-wide cursor effect), the illustration set, and the cloud-textured wordmark.\n\n### godly.design — Mood board\n\nCurated posts of interface interaction clips. Inspiration only; it is not a dependency and has no code or package implications.\n\n- Borrow: spring feel, press states and motion patterns, captured as written notes in the motion spec before any coding.\n- Do not borrow: whole layouts, or any effect that needs a mouse.\n\n## Launch gates\n\n- Mobile Lighthouse performance at least 90 and accessibility at least 95.\n- Initial JavaScript at most 150 kB gzipped (relaxed from a stricter 120 kB because the stack probe measured about 139 kB before real content; code-split to stay under).\n- LCP at most 2.5 s and CLS under 0.1.\n- WCAG 2.2 AA.\n- Full `prefers-reduced-motion` support.\n\n## Content principles\n\n- The resume PDF is the source of truth; on any conflict it wins over the old site. Items the resume does not cover are kept from the old site.\n- The same six sections as before: About Me, Skills, Education, Experience, Projects, Contact Me.\n- The phone number is never published, in site copy, the served resume, meta tags, JSON-LD or Open Graph data. The served resume is a phone-stripped copy.\n- Public email, GPA and the DJ Instagram link stay public (D-11).\n","numLines":103,"startLine":1,"totalLines":103}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01JPhkZmZnDuQ4Gw2cSTxhTJ","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

Plan 01-04 added candidates B and C, the full 19-pair list for every section, the type pairing per candidate, and, after the user picked candidate A (tuned seed indigo, Inter only), the chosen system below.\n8\t\n9\tOwner decisions this file records: D-04 (three candidates, per-theme tokens, the user picks one), D-05 (type explored with color), D-06 (exactly 5 role tokens plus derived tints). WCAG 2.2 AA is the bar.\n10\t\n11\t## Format\n12\t\n13\tTokens live in fenced blocks so a script can recompute every contrast ratio from the OKLCH values instead of trusting the author. There are three block types, identified by the fence info string:\n14\t\n15\t- `palette X` (X is one capital letter) holds one palette. Each line is a theme, a token name and an OKLCH color, for example `light --text oklch(L C H)`, where L is lightness from 0 to 1, C is chroma and H is hue in degrees. THEME is `light` or `dark`. Every palette must define exactly the five role tokens for both themes (10 lines). A palette block may also carry derived-override lines (a `mix()` formula) when one palette needs a different derived formula than the shared one.\n16\t- `derived` holds tints computed from the roles. Each line is a theme, a token name and `mix(--a P%, --b)`, which matches CSS `color-mix(in oklch, var(--a) P%, var(--b))`: lightness and chroma blend linearly, hue goes along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color takes the other color's hue. A derived token may never be given a literal color. That is what makes a palette swap a single-block edit (D-06): only the five role lines change, and every derived token follows.\n17\t- `pairs` holds the contrast matrix. Each line is `FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY`, where CATEGORY is `text` (needs 4.5:1), `large` (3:1), `ui` (3:1) or `focus` (3:1), and USED-BY names the section anchor and the element. Every pair is evaluated for every palette in both themes.\n18\t\n19\tA final line `Chosen palette: X` (written once the user picks) names the palette that ships. It is written as plain text on its own line, outside any fence.\n20\t\n21\tVerify with `node contrast-check.mjs 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md` from this directory. The last line is `RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M` and the exit code is 0 only when every pair passes. Add `--require-chosen` once the choice is made. `--convert VALUE` turns a hex into OKLCH (rounded to stay inside the sRGB gamut) or an OKLCH into a hex, and is how role values and realtimecolors links are authored. `--selftest` proves the checker against independently computed ratios.\n22\t\n23\tRatios are compared unrounded against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to two decimals. A color outside the sRGB gamut fails its rows as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because the browser would remap it and the ratio would no longer be the one that was checked.\n24\t\n25\t## Role tokens\n26\t\n27\tThe five roles follow the realtimecolors order. Per-theme values are mandatory (D-04): the seed indigo `2f27ce` measures 2.23:1 on the dark background `050315`, which fails text, UI and focus use.\n28\t\n29\t| Order | Token | Job |\n30\t|-------|-------|-----|\n31\t| 1 | `--text` | Body and heading text, and the on-color for filled dark surfaces |\n32\t| 2 | `--background` | Page background |\n33\t| 3 | `--primary` | Filled buttons, the main brand fill |\n34\t| 4 | `--secondary` | Tint family for cards and soft fills (decorative, never text or a border on its own: `dedcff` on the light background is 1.29:1) |\n35\t| 5 | `--accent` | Highlights and large display color |\n36\t\n37\tDerived tokens (D-06), all `mix()` of roles, defined once for every candidate in the shared `derived` block:\n38\t\n39\t| Token | Job |\n40\t|-------|-----|\n41\t| `--surface` | Card, toast and overlay panel fill |\n42\t| `--muted` | Dates, captions and secondary copy |\n43\t| `--border` | Decorative hairlines (no contrast requirement) |\n44\t| `--border-strong` | Control boundaries (3:1) |\n45\t| `--link` | Inline link text |\n46\t| `--on-primary` | Label on a filled primary button |\n47\t| `--on-accent` | Label on an accent chip or active pill |\n48\t| `--primary-hover` | Hovered or pressed filled button |\n49\t| `--focus-ring` | Keyboard focus indicator |\n50\t\n51\t## Candidate A — Tuned seed indigo\n52\t\n53\tChosen in Phase 1; superseded by candidate D in Phase 3 (D-02). One tune from the seed in light: `--primary` moves from `2f27ce` to `5046e5` (plan 01-01 had first tuned it to `281fb4`; the full 19-pair set forces a second move). Reason: a focus ring must hold 3:1 against the page, a card, the secondary tint and a filled primary button. With `281fb4` no ring color does all four: a mid-tone ring clears the button but gives 2.50:1 on the secondary tint, and a near-black ring gives 1.89:1 on the button. A primary lighter than the seed's (relative luminance about 0.11 to 0.18) opens the band: a near-black ring then reads on the button (3.2:1 or better) and on every light surface, while the white label on the button still holds 4.5:1. B and C override it inside their palette blocks. `--on-primary` and `--on-accent` are the page background in both themes (a light label on the deep light fills, a dark label on the lifted dark fills). `--primary-hover` is the primary pulled slightly toward the text color in light and toward the background in dark (mixing a lifted dark primary toward near-white leaves the gamut), so the button always reads as pressed in. `--focus-ring` is the text color in both themes: it is the only color that holds 3:1 against the page, a card, the secondary tint and a filled primary at once, once the light primary sits in the band described under candidate A.\n116\t\n117\t```derived\n118\tlight --surface mix(--secondary 30%, --background)\n119\tdark --surface mix(--secondary 60%, --background)\n120\tlight --muted mix(--text 70%, --background)\n121\tdark --muted mix(--text 72%, --background)\n122\tlight --border mix(--text 14%, --background)\n123\tdark --border mix(--text 16%, --background)\n124\tlight --border-strong mix(--text 55%, --background)\n125\tdark --border-strong mix(--text 55%, --background)\n126\tlight --link mix(--primary 80%, --text)\n127\tdark --link mix(--accent 100%, --background)\n128\tlight --on-primary mix(--background 100%, --text)\n129\tdark --on-primary mix(--background 100%, --text)\n130\tlight --on-accent mix(--background 100%, --text)\n131\tdark --on-accent mix(--background 100%, --text)\n132\tlight --primary-hover mix(--primary 85%, --text)\n133\tdark --primary-hover mix(--primary 94%, --background)\n134\tlight --focus-ring mix(--text 100%, --background)\n135\tdark --focus-ring mix(--text 100%, --background)\n136\t```\n137\t\n138\t## Candidate B — Clay and cream\n139\t\n140\tNot chosen.\n141\t\n142\tWarm clay on cream. It carries no contrast requirement and is never the only cue for a control boundary; controls use `--border-strong` (3:1).\n356\t- Disabled controls are exempt under WCAG 1.4.3, but they still get a non-color cue (reduced weight plus a \"not available\" affordance such as a dashed outline), not color alone.\n357\t- `--secondary` is a fill. It is never used as text or as a lone border.\n358\t\n359\t## Chosen system\n360\t\n361\tCandidate D, neutral grounds with the tuned seed indigo as signal (Phase 3, D-02; the Phase 1 pick was candidate A, which stays recorded above). Plan 01-04 added candidates B and C, the full 19-pair list for every section, the type pairing per candidate, and, after the user picked candidate A (tuned seed indigo, Inter only), the chosen system below.\n\nOwner decisions this file records: D-04 (three candidates, per-theme tokens, the user picks one), D-05 (type explored with color), D-06 (exactly 5 role tokens plus derived tints). WCAG 2.2 AA is the bar.\n\n## Format\n\nTokens live in fenced blocks so a script can recompute every contrast ratio from the OKLCH values instead of trusting the author. There are three block types, identified by the fence info string:\n\n- `palette X` (X is one capital letter) holds one palette. Each line is a theme, a token name and an OKLCH color, for example `light --text oklch(L C H)`, where L is lightness from 0 to 1, C is chroma and H is hue in degrees. THEME is `light` or `dark`. Every palette must define exactly the five role tokens for both themes (10 lines). A palette block may also carry derived-override lines (a `mix()` formula) when one palette needs a different derived formula than the shared one.\n- `derived` holds tints computed from the roles. Each line is a theme, a token name and `mix(--a P%, --b)`, which matches CSS `color-mix(in oklch, var(--a) P%, var(--b))`: lightness and chroma blend linearly, hue goes along the shorter arc, and an achromatic color takes the other color's hue. A derived token may never be given a literal color. That is what makes a palette swap a single-block edit (D-06): only the five role lines change, and every derived token follows.\n- `pairs` holds the contrast matrix. Each line is `FG on BG CATEGORY USED-BY`, where CATEGORY is `text` (needs 4.5:1), `large` (3:1), `ui` (3:1) or `focus` (3:1), and USED-BY names the section anchor and the element. Every pair is evaluated for every palette in both themes.\n\nA final line `Chosen palette: X` (written once the user picks) names the palette that ships. It is written as plain text on its own line, outside any fence.\n\nVerify with `node contrast-check.mjs 01-DESIGN-TOKENS.md` from this directory. The last line is `RESULT: PASS palettes=N checks=M` and the exit code is 0 only when every pair passes. Add `--require-chosen` once the choice is made. `--convert VALUE` turns a hex into OKLCH (rounded to stay inside the sRGB gamut) or an OKLCH into a hex, and is how role values and realtimecolors links are authored. `--selftest` proves the checker against independently computed ratios.\n\nRatios are compared unrounded against the threshold (4.499 fails 4.5) and printed to two decimals. A color outside the sRGB gamut fails its rows as OUT-OF-GAMUT, because the browser would remap it and the ratio would no longer be the one that was checked.\n\n## Role tokens\n\nThe five roles follow the realtimecolors order. Per-theme values are mandatory (D-04): the seed indigo `2f27ce` measures 2.23:1 on the dark background `050315`, which fails text, UI and focus use.\n\n| Order | Token | Job |\n|-------|-------|-----|\n| 1 | `--text` | Body and heading text, and the on-color for filled dark surfaces |\n| 2 | `--background` | Page background |\n| 3 | `--primary` | Filled buttons, the main brand fill |\n| 4 | `--secondary` | Tint family for cards and soft fills (decorative, never text or a border on its own: `dedcff` on the light background is 1.29:1) |\n| 5 | `--accent` | Highlights and large display color |\n\nDerived tokens (D-06), all `mix()` of roles, defined once for every candidate in the shared `derived` block:\n\n| Token | Job |\n|-------|-----|\n| `--surface` | Card, toast and overlay panel fill |\n| `--muted` | Dates, captions and secondary copy |\n| `--border` | Decorative hairlines (no contrast requirement) |\n| `--border-strong` | Control boundaries (3:1) |\n| `--link` | Inline link text |\n| `--on-primary` | Label on a filled primary button |\n| `--on-accent` | Label on an accent chip or active pill |\n| `--primary-hover` | Hovered or pressed filled button |\n| `--focus-ring` | Keyboard focus indicator |\n\n## Candidate A — Tuned seed indigo\n\nChosen in Phase 1; superseded by candidate D in Phase 3 (D-02). Kept here as the recorded fallback.\n\nContinuity with the realtimecolors seed (050315 / fbfbfe / 2f27ce / dedcff / 433bff). Dark roles are authored for dark, not inverted: the text and background swap ends, primary and accent lift to the 5.66:1 and 8.19:1 class on `050315`, and secondary becomes a dark indigo tint. One tune from the seed in light: `--primary` moves from `2f27ce` to `5046e5` (plan 01-01 had first tuned it to `281fb4`; the full 19-pair set forces a second move). Reason: a focus ring must hold 3:1 against the page, a card, the secondary tint and a filled primary button. With `281fb4` no ring color does all four: a mid-tone ring clears the button but gives 2.50:1 on the secondary tint, and a near-black ring gives 1.89:1 on the button. A primary lighter than the seed's (relative luminance about 0.11 to 0.18) opens the band: a near-black ring then reads on the button (3.2:1 or better) and on every light surface, while the white label on the button still holds 4.5:1. Cost: primary `5046e5` and accent `433bff` are now close in light, so color alone never separates them (Pitfall 5); state uses shape and weight too.\n\nType pairing: Inter variable for display and body, one family: `@fontsource-variable/inter` 5.3.0. Bricolage Grotesque is a variable grotesque with quirky, slightly condensed shapes and an optical size axis, characterful at display size and still clean for short headings.\n\nSwatches (hex of the OKLCH roles below, for reference):\n\n| Role | Light | Dark |\n|------|-------|------|\n| --text | #04211f | #effaf7 |\n| --background | #f3fbf9 | #04191a |\n| --primary | #0f766e | #0b9e91 |\n| --secondary | #c9efe6 | #0c3a3a |\n| --accent | #b45309 | #f0b050 |\n\n```palette C\nlight --text oklch(0.2255 0.0347 188.59)\nlight --background oklch(0.9815 0.0088 179.61)\nlight --primary oklch(0.5109 0.0860 186.39)\nlight --secondary oklch(0.9226 0.0412 179.41)\nlight --accent oklch(0.5553 0.1455 49.00)\ndark --text oklch(0.9761 0.0122 178.03)\ndark --background oklch(0.1965 0.0277 199.29)\ndark --primary oklch(0.6300 0.1100 184)\ndark --secondary oklch(0.3187 0.0478 195.02)\ndark --accent oklch(0.7997 0.1339 74.64)\ndark --link mix(--primary 75%, --text)\n```\n\nDerived overrides: dark `--link` follows the lifted primary (`mix(--primary 75%, --text)`) instead of the accent, so links stay teal in both themes. Teal with an amber accent is lively without being loud, and the contrast between cool fields and a warm accent gives the page a clear second voice for highlights, scroll-spy and active pills. Bricolage Grotesque adds personality in headings while the sans stays modern and quick to read (Crafted, Fast). It is less Warm than B and less continuous with the seed than A. Teal is a common design-engineer choice, so identity depends more on motion and layout than on color.\n\nContrast results:\n\n| Pair | Category | Light | Dark |\n|------|----------|-------|------|\n| --text on --background | text | 16.08 | 16.98 |\n| --text on --surface | text | 15.29 | 13.98 |\n| --text on --secondary | text | 13.66 | 11.71 |\n| --muted on --background | text | 6.91 | 8.42 |\n| --muted on --surface | text | 6.57 | 6.93 |\n| --link on --background | text | 6.66 | 7.48 |\n| --link on --surface | text | 6.34 | 6.16 |\n| --on-primary on --primary | text | 5.21 | 5.45 |\n| --on-primary on --primary-hover | text | 6.30 | 4.89 |\n| --on-accent on --accent | text | 4.78 | 9.52 |\n| --border-strong on --background | ui | 4.26 | 5.14 |\n| --border-strong on --surface | ui | 4.05 | 4.23 |\n| --primary on --background | ui | 5.21 | 5.45 |\n| --accent on --background | ui | 4.78 | 9.52 |\n| --accent on --surface | ui | 4.54 | 7.83 |\n| --focus-ring on --background | focus | 16.08 | 16.98 |\n| --focus-ring on --surface | focus | 15.29 | 13.98 |\n| --focus-ring on --primary | focus | 3.09 | 3.12 |\n| --focus-ring on --secondary | focus | 13.66 | 11.71 |\n\n## Candidate D — Neutral grounds, indigo as signal\n\nChosen (Phase 3, D-02). It carries no contrast requirement and is never the only cue for a control boundary; controls use `--border-strong` (3:1).\n- Disabled controls are exempt under WCAG 1.4.3, but they still get a non-color cue (reduced weight plus a \"not available\" affordance such as a dashed outline), not color alone.\n- `--secondary` is a fill. It is never used as text or as a lone border.\n\n## Chosen system\n\nCandidate D, neutral grounds with the tuned seed indigo as signal (Phase 3, D-02; the Phase 1 pick was candidate A, which stays recorded above). Headings never change width between themes.\n- Selection: `::selection` uses `--primary` with `--on-primary`.\n\nLadder (`--text-mega` through `--text-xs`, replacing `--text-xs` through `--text-5xl`). Fluid steps are `clamp(min, intercept + slope vw, max)`; the rem part of each clamp keeps browser text zoom effective (WCAG 1.4.4). Each step carries `--line-height`, `--letter-spacing` and `--font-weight` modifiers, so one utility class (for example `text-xl`) sets all four.\n\n| Token | Size | Line height | Tracking | Weight | Use |\n|-------|------|-------------|----------|--------|-----|\n| `--text-mega` | `var(--t-mega)`, below 768 px `clamp(3.75rem, 0.9rem + 22vw, 6.75rem)`, at 768 px and up `clamp(3.75rem, 0.9rem + 12.2vw, 12rem)` | 0.86 | -0.045em | 800 | Hero h1 poster name |\n| `--text-xl` | `clamp(2.5rem, 1.4rem + 4.8vw, 5.5rem)` | 0.95 | -0.03em | 750 | Section h2 |\n| `--text-l` | `clamp(1.5rem, 1.2rem + 1.4vw, 2.5rem)` | 1.15 | -0.015em | 500 | Role line, lead paragraphs |\n| `--text-m` | `clamp(1.2rem, 1.1rem + 0.4vw, 1.45rem)` | 1.35 | -0.005em | 600 | Card titles, nav wordmark |\n| `--text-body` | `clamp(1rem, 0.96rem + 0.2vw, 1.0625rem)` | 1.55 | 0 | 400 | Body copy |\n| `--text-s` | 0.875rem | 1.45 | 0.005em | 500 | Dates, card metadata, nav labels |\n| `--text-xs` | 0.8125rem | 1.4 | 0.01em | 500 | Captions, chip labels (never below this) |\n\n`--t-mega` is a custom property set on `:root` in `base.css`, with the 768 px media step there (never in `tokens.css`, which stays flat). Both clamps give 6.75rem at 768 px, so there is no jump at the breakpoint. The phone override (a steeper 22vw slope capped at 6.75rem) is what fits the name, role line and both CTAs into the 375 x 667 first viewport (NAV-04).\n\n## Spacing, radius, elevation, z-index and breakpoints\n\n- Spacing: Tailwind v4 default base `--spacing: 0.25rem`; all spacing uses the default scale (no custom steps). Minimum touch target 44 by 44 px (`size-11`) for interactive controls.\n- Radius (Phase 3, D-06, hold versus press): held things are 4 px (`--radius-hold`, utility `rounded-hold`); pressed things are 9999 px (`--radius-pill`, `rounded-pill`); the one declared exception is the expanded pill panel at 28 px (`--radius-panel`, `rounded-panel`). `--radius-sm`, `--radius-md` and `--radius-lg` are deleted. `cn()` teaches tailwind-merge the custom size and radius utility names so they merge correctly.\n- Elevation (per theme, set on `:root` and `[data-theme=dark]`; shadows are decorative, so they carry no contrast requirement; edges that matter use `--border` or `--border-strong`):\n\n| Token | Light | Dark |\n|-------|-------|------|\n| `--shadow-sm` | `0 1px 2px color-mix(in oklch, var(--text) 10%, transparent)` | `0 1px 2px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.5)` |\n| `--shadow-md` | `0 4px 12px color-mix(in oklch, var(--text) 12%, transparent)` | `0 4px 12px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.55)` |\n| `--shadow-lg` | `0 12px 32px color-mix(in oklch, var(--text) 16%, transparent)` | `0 12px 32px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.65)` |\n\n- z-index layers (`--z-*`): base 0, rail-lift 10, sticky-nav 40, pill-nav 50, overlay-backdrop 60, overlay 70, toast 80, skip-link 90. The skip link is the top layer so it is never covered when it takes focus.\n- Breakpoints (mobile first, min-width): 375 baseline (design target, no media query), `md` 768 (`48rem`), `lg` 1024 (`64rem`), `xl` 1280 (`80rem`). These match the Tailwind v4 defaults for md, lg and xl, so no override is needed beyond documenting 375 as the smallest supported width.\n\n## Tailwind v4 mapping\n\n- Theme switch: `html` carries a `data-theme` attribute (`light` or `dark`), set by an inline script in `<head>` before first paint. `color-scheme` is set per theme.\n- Dark variant: `@custom-variant dark (&:where([data-theme=dark], [data-theme=dark] *));`\n- Role and derived tokens live as plain CSS variables in `tokens.css`: ten role values per theme (the single edit block) and nine derived tokens written as `color-mix(in oklch, var(--a) P%, var(--b))`, matching the `mix()` formulas in the Chosen system table. No HTML sketches.\n8\t\n9\t## Section registry\n10\t\n11\tSeven fixed anchors. Every phase doc refers to a section by its anchor, never by a position number. it is the first thing below the fold and one pill tap from anywhere.     |\n29\t| 3     | Projects   | {#projects}   | The signature rail and overlay; it follows Experience so the work sits next to the roles it came from.         |\n30\t| 4     | About Me   | {#about}      | Personality (the DJ side) comes after the evidence, and links to the Instagram in Contact.                     |\n31\t| 5     | Skills     | {#skills}     | A scan-friendly summary once the reader knows the work.                                                        |\n32\t| 6     | Education  | {#education}  | Short, factual, needed for the GPA and degree check, but rarely the first stop.                                |\n33\t| 7     | Contact Me | {#contact}    | The page ends on the action; it is also one tap from the hero CTA and the pill nav.                            |\n34\t\n35\t## Navigation model\n36\t\n37\t- 768 px and wider use a sticky top nav, always visible, on a solid ground (D-18): the wordmark top left (PHAN in the light theme, PHVNTM in the dark theme; it is the home link), the six section links (Experience, Projects, About, Skills, Education, Contact), the theme toggle [IX-10] and a Resume button, with a scroll-spy indicator under the active link [IX-08]. The bottom pill is not shown at this width.\n38\t- Below 768 px a non-fixed top bar sits above the hero (D-19): the wordmark on the left and the theme toggle on the right, visible on first paint. A thumb-reachable bottom pill nav is fixed to the viewport. Collapsed, it has three segments: Experience, Projects and Menu. Experience and Projects jump straight to their section; the Menu segment morphs the pill in place into a panel of the six section links, the theme toggle and Resume [IX-07] (reference 445). The panel carries Contact Me.\n39\t- A skip link is the first focusable element and targets {#main}.\n40\t- Nav form is chosen by width. Hover effects are chosen by pointer capability, never by width.\n41\t- Nav links are plain anchors in a single page: there is no router, and the URL changes only by the browser's own hash handling.\n42\t\n43\t## Recruiter fast path (10-second test)\n44\t\n45\tA first-time visitor on a 375 px phone reaches each item with at most one tap from the first viewport.\n46\t\n47\t| Item       | Where at 375                                                    | Taps from first viewport |\n48\t| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |\n49\t| Name       | The h1 in the hero, visible on first paint                      | 0                        |\n50\t| Role       | The role line directly under the name                           | 0                        |\n51\t| Experience | The Experience segment of the collapsed pill nav                | 1                        |\n52\t| Projects   | The Projects segment of the collapsed pill nav                  | 1                        |\n53\t| Resume     | The Download resume CTA in the hero                             | 1                        |\n54\t| Contact    | The Copy email CTA in the hero (Contact Me is in the pill menu) | 1                        |\n55\t\n56\tPass rule: all six found in 10 seconds or less, timed on a real phone with motion enabled (the same rule as the design brief).\n57\t\n58\t## Above the fold @ 375\n59\t\n60\tA 375 x 667 viewport shows, top to bottom:\n61\t\n62\t- The top bar with the wordmark and the theme toggle.\n63\t- The name as the h1, \"Aaron\" over \"Phan\".\n64\t- The role line under it, plain text from first paint (the text effect [IX-01] arrives in Phase 5).\n65\t- The Download resume and Copy email CTAs, each at least 44 px tall. There is no Contact link in the hero.\n66\t- The two corner facts under the CTAs: \"Graduating December 2026, UT Austin ECE\" and \"Last role: Capital One, summer 2026\".\n67\t- The collapsed pill nav fixed at the bottom, clear of the CTAs.\n68\t- The top edge of {#experience}, so the reader knows there is more below.\n69\t\n70\tThe frame is `### Frame: Hero @ 375`. Nothing in the first viewport depends on JavaScript or motion.\n71\t\n72\t## Anchors and landmarks\n73\t\n74\t- Landmarks: header (skip link and nav), nav, main {#main}, footer.\n75\t- One h1 per page: the name in the hero. Every other section has one h2, and each section element is labelled by its heading with `aria-labelledby`.\n76\t- Section anchors are the seven in the registry above; nav links and CTAs are plain `<a href=\"#anchor\">`.\n77\t- Each section carries `scroll-margin-top` equal to the sticky nav height at 768 px and up, and the height of the safe top area at 375, so a link jump never hides a heading.\n78\t\n79\t## Project rail and overlay behavior\n80\t\n81\tFeatured order: PRJ-01, PRJ-02, PRJ-03, then PRJ-04, PRJ-05, PRJ-06, PRJ-07 (the remaining projects, newest first).\n82\t\n83\t- The rail is native horizontal scrolling with scroll-snap on touch [IX-04] and a hover lift with neighbor shift on a fine pointer [IX-03], with the same lift on keyboard focus [IX-06].\n84\t- Opening a project shows an overlay with the index written as NN / 07. Prev and next wrap around (07 / 07 goes to 01 / 07). The overlay has a Close button; Escape closes it; focus returns to the rail item that opened it; the URL does not change (deep-linkable project URLs are a deferred requirement).\n85\t- Dialog accessibility is settled by ADR-0006: focus trap, inert background, scroll lock and focus return belong to the dialog primitive, and motion animates only the morph [IX-05].\n86\t- Project links and images are deferred (G-01, G-02), so overlay links show only when supplied and rail cards use a cover placeholder.\n87\t\n88\t## Global behaviors\n89\t\n90\t- Press-squish [IX-02] on all buttons and cards, on the inner surface only.\n91\t- Section reveals [IX-15] when a section enters the viewport; content is visible by default and the hidden start state is set after mount.\n92\t- Desktop smooth wheel scroll [IX-16], off on touch and under reduced motion.\n93\t- Desktop pointer polish [IX-17]: Tilt on the About photo, Magnetic on the hero and contact CTA wrappers, Spotlight on experience cards, fine pointer only.\n94\t\n95\t## Frame conventions\n96\t\n97\t- Frames are drawn in a fenced `text` block with printable ASCII only. The width counts the whole line including both `|` borders: 38 characters for 375 px, 64 for 768 px and 96 for 1280 px (so the inner width is 36, 62 and 94).\n98\t- Square-bracket annotations name an interaction ID from `01-MOTION-SPEC.md` (for example [IX-09]) or an anchor (for example [#contact]).\n99\t- `[ Label ]` is a button. `Label >` is a link. `(( ))` marks the toast. `=====` borders the bottom pill nav and its expanded panel on mobile. `#` borders mark a visible focus ring. `:::` marks a blurred backdrop. `( )` around a word is a chip, `[logo]` and `[ O ]` are logo and monogram chips.\n100\t- Touch targets are at least 44 px high and wide at 375 px.\n101\t- The fixed bottom pill is drawn only where it matters (Hero, Contact, the nav states); the sticky top nav is drawn in the Hero frames and the nav state frames. Dates in frames use an ASCII hyphen; on the site they are written with an en dash per the date policy in the inventory.\n102\t- Copy in frames is abbreviated where it does not fit (for example short month names at 375).
