Plan 01-07 set the final section order and added the hero, nav, rail, overlay and every other section at 375, 768 and 1280 px.\n\nWireframes are ASCII inside this markdown file (D-02). No HTML sketches.\n\n## Section registry\n\nSeven fixed anchors. Every phase doc refers to a section by its anchor, never by a position number. The page order is in the next section.\n\n| Anchor        | Section    |\n| ------------- | ---------- |\n| {#hero}       | Hero       |\n| {#experience} | Experience |\n| {#projects}   | Projects   |\n| {#about}      | About Me   |\n| {#skills}     | Skills     |\n| {#education}  | Education  |\n| {#contact}    | Contact Me |\n\n## Section order\n\n| Order | Section    | Anchor        | Why here                                                                                                       |\n| ----- | ---------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| 1     | Hero       | {#hero}       | Name, role and the Resume and Copy email CTAs are visible at first paint, which is most of the 10-second test. |\n| 2     | Experience | {#experience} | Recruiters look for experience first; it is the first thing below the fold and one pill tap from anywhere.     |\n| 3     | Projects   | {#projects}   | The signature rail and overlay; it follows Experience so the work sits next to the roles it came from.         |\n| 4     | About Me   | {#about}      | Personality (the DJ side) comes after the evidence, and links to the Instagram in Contact.                     |\n| 5     | Skills     | {#skills}     | A scan-friendly summary once the reader knows the work.                                                        |\n| 6     | Education  | {#education}  | Short, factual, needed for the GPA and degree check, but rarely the first stop.                                |\n| 7     | Contact Me | {#contact}    | The page ends on the action; it is also one tap from the hero CTA and the pill nav.                            |\n\n## Navigation model\n\n- 768 px and wider use a sticky top nav, always visible, on a solid ground (D-18): the wordmark top left (PHAN in the light theme, PHVNTM in the dark theme; it is the home link), the six section links (Experience, Projects, About, Skills, Education, Contact), the theme toggle [IX-10] and a Resume button, with a scroll-spy indicator under the active link [IX-08]. The bottom pill is not shown at this width.\n- Below 768 px a non-fixed top bar sits above the hero (D-19): the wordmark on the left and the theme toggle on the right, visible on first paint. A thumb-reachable bottom pill nav is fixed to the viewport. Collapsed, it has three segments: Experience, Projects and Menu. Experience and Projects jump straight to their section; the Menu segment morphs the pill in place into a panel of the six section links, the theme toggle and Resume [IX-07] (reference 445). The panel carries Contact Me.\n- A skip link is the first focusable element and targets {#main}.\n- Nav form is chosen by width. Hover effects are chosen by pointer capability, never by width.\n- Nav links are plain anchors in a single page: there is no router, and the URL changes only by the browser's own hash handling.\n\n## Recruiter fast path (10-second test)\n\nA first-time visitor on a 375 px phone reaches each item with at most one tap from the first viewport.\n\n| Item       | Where at 375                                                    | Taps from first viewport |\n| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |\n| Name       | The h1 in the hero, visible on first paint                      | 0                        |\n| Role       | The role line directly under the name                           | 0                        |\n| Experience | The Experience segment of the collapsed pill nav                | 1                        |\n| Projects   | The Projects segment of the collapsed pill nav                  | 1                        |\n| Resume     | The Download resume CTA in the hero                             | 1                        |\n| Contact    | The Copy email CTA in the hero (Contact Me is in the pill menu) | 1                        |\n\nPass rule: all six found in 10 seconds or less, timed on a real phone with motion enabled (the same rule as the design brief).\n\n## Above the fold @ 375\n\nA 375 x 667 viewport shows, top to bottom:\n\n- The top bar with the wordmark and the theme toggle.\n- The name as the h1, \"Aaron\" over \"Phan\".\n- The role line under it, plain text from first paint (the text effect [IX-01] arrives in Phase 5).\n- The Download resume and Copy email CTAs, each at least 44 px tall. There is no Contact link in the hero.\n- The two corner facts under the CTAs: \"Graduating December 2026, UT Austin ECE\" and \"Last role: Capital One, summer 2026\".\n- The collapsed pill nav fixed at the bottom, clear of the CTAs.\n- The top edge of {#experience}, so the reader knows there is more below.\n\nThe frame is `### Frame: Hero @ 375`. Nothing in the first viewport depends on JavaScript or motion.\n\n## Anchors and landmarks\n\n- Landmarks: header (skip link and nav), nav, main {#main}, footer.\n- One h1 per page: the name in the hero. Every other section has one h2, and each section element is labelled by its heading with `aria-labelledby`.\n- Section anchors are the seven in the registry above; nav links and CTAs are plain `<a href=\"#anchor\">`.\n- Each section carries `scroll-margin-top` equal to the sticky nav height at 768 px and up, and the height of the safe top area at 375, so a link jump never hides a heading.\n\n## Project rail and overlay behavior\n\nFeatured order: PRJ-01, PRJ-02, PRJ-03, then PRJ-04, PRJ-05, PRJ-06, PRJ-07 (the remaining projects, newest first).\n\n- The rail is native horizontal scrolling with scroll-snap on touch [IX-04] and a hover lift with neighbor shift on a fine pointer [IX-03], with the same lift on keyboard focus [IX-06].\n- Opening a project shows an overlay with the index written as NN / 07. Prev and next wrap around (07 / 07 goes to 01 / 07). The overlay has a Close button; Escape closes it; focus returns to the rail item that opened it; the URL does not change (deep-linkable project URLs are a deferred requirement).\n- Dialog accessibility is settled by ADR-0006: focus trap, inert background, scroll lock and focus return belong to the dialog primitive, and motion animates only the morph [IX-05].\n- Project links and images are deferred (G-01, G-02), so overlay links show only when supplied and rail cards use a cover placeholder.\n\n## Global behaviors\n\n- Press-squish [IX-02] on all buttons and cards, on the inner surface only.\n- Section reveals [IX-15] when a section enters the viewport; content is visible by default and the hidden start state is set after mount.\n- Desktop smooth wheel scroll [IX-16], off on touch and under reduced motion.\n- Desktop pointer polish [IX-17]: Tilt on the About photo, Magnetic on the hero and contact CTA wrappers, Spotlight on experience cards, fine pointer only.\n\n## Frame conventions\n\n- Frames are drawn in a fenced `text` block with printable ASCII only. The width counts the whole line including both `|` borders: 38 characters for 375 px, 64 for 768 px and 96 for 1280 px (so the inner width is 36, 62 and 94).\n- Square-bracket annotations name an interaction ID from `01-MOTION-SPEC.md` (for example [IX-09]) or an anchor (for example [#contact]).\n- `[ Label ]` is a button. `Label >` is a link. `(( ))` marks the toast. `=====` borders the bottom pill nav and its expanded panel on mobile. `#` borders mark a visible focus ring. `:::` marks a blurred backdrop. `( )` around a word is a chip, `[logo]` and `[ O ]` are logo and monogram chips.\n- Touch targets are at least 44 px high and wide at 375 px.\n- The fixed bottom pill is drawn only where it matters (Hero, Contact, the nav states); the sticky top nav is drawn in the Hero frames and the nav state frames. Dates in frames use an ASCII hyphen; on the site they are written with an en dash per the date policy in the inventory.\n- Copy in frames is abbreviated where it does not fit (for example short month names at 375). {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HUQs3Zb675DzMcucphzGr9","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Motion Spec (DOC-05)\n2\t\n3\tStatus: Accepted\n4\t\n5\tPhase 1 plan 01-01 seeded this file with the ownership rule, the fixed 17-row interaction catalog and the first fully specified interaction (IX-09). Plan 01-05 completed it: principles, tokens, reduced-motion layers, ownership matrix, vendored primitives, the other 16 interaction specs and the element ownership check.\n6\t\n7\t## Ownership rule\n8\t\n9\t- Exactly one library animates any element: motion, react-spring, CSS or Lenis. Never two on the same element or property.\n10\t- No Tailwind transition utilities on an element a library animates.\n11\t- react-spring is scoped to IX-02, IX-03, IX-06 and IX-10 (velocity-carrying, tactile physics). Everything else uses motion, CSS or Lenis as the catalog says.\n12\t\n13\t## Principles\n14\t\n15\t- Motion never gates content. Name, role and CTAs are visible at first paint. The hero text effect runs only on the role line and never delays it.\n16\t- Animate transform and opacity only, plus motion layout animations where an interaction needs them (IX-05, IX-07, IX-08, IX-11, IX-14).\n17\t- Fine-pointer effects are gated by the media query `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and carry no hover-only content (MOT-04). Touch gets a tap or press equivalent, or nothing.\n18\t- `touch-action` is set only on small draggables. The project rail uses native horizontal scrolling, so vertical page scroll is never captured.\n19\t- Infinite or looping motion pauses when off-screen or when the tab is hidden.\n20\t- Motion budget: entrance animations take at most 420 ms; stagger is at most 60 ms per item for at most 6 items; nothing blocks input.\n21\t\n22\t## Motion tokens\n23\t\n24\tCanonical home is `src/anim/tokens.ts`, with CSS mirrors `--dur-fast`, `--dur-base`, `--dur-slow` and `--ease-out`. One table drives both libraries so they feel like one system.\n25\t\n26\t| Token | Kind | motion format (stiffness, damping, mass) | react-spring format (tension, friction, mass) | Value |\n27\t|-------|------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|\n28\t| snappy | spring | 500, 32, 1 | 500, 32, 1 | presses, toggles |\n29\t| gentle | spring | 170, 26, 1 | 170, 26, 1 | rail lift, layout settling |\n30\t| bouncy | spring | 300, 14, 1 | 300, 14, 1 | playful overshoot, used sparingly |\n31\t| fast | duration | n/a | n/a | 120 ms |\n32\t| base | duration | n/a | n/a | 220 ms |\n33\t| slow | duration | n/a | n/a | 420 ms |\n34\t| ease-out | easing | n/a | n/a | cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) |\n35\t\n36\treact-spring `tension` equals motion `stiffness` and `friction` equals `damping`. The spring numbers are starting values, to be tuned on a real iPhone and a real Android phone during the signature-rail work (Phase 4).\n37\t\n38\t## Reduced motion\n39\t\n40\tOne preference source (MOT-01): `useMotionPreference` reads `prefers-reduced-motion` with a `change` listener (users toggle it live) and feeds three consumers:\n41\t\n42\t- motion: `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (from `motion/react`).\n43\t- react-spring: `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` from `@react-spring/web`, set in an effect with a dependency array and a cleanup that resets it.\n44\t- CSS: the guard `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, which also gates smooth scroll behind `no-preference`.\n45\t\n46\tLenis is not started under reduced motion (MOT-05). Motion's `user` mode still animates opacity, so text effects and other opacity-driven wrappers branch manually on the hook's `reduced` value.\n47\t\n48\t| Layer | Mechanism | Covers |\n49\t|-------|-----------|--------|\n50\t| L0 Progressive enhancement | Content is visible by default in HTML and CSS. Reveal wrappers set the hidden initial state only after mount on the client, and `<noscript>` guarantees visibility. | JS failure, slow hydration, crawlers, screenshots |\n51\t| L1 CSS guard | `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` collapses animation and transition durations to near zero, runs animations once and sets `scroll-behavior: auto`. | CSS transitions, keyframes, anchor scroll |\n52\t| L2 motion | `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (\"user\", or \"always\" and \"never\" from an override). Disables transform and layout animations, keeps opacity and color. | All motion components, including vendored primitives |\n53\t| L3 react-spring | `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` in the provider effect. Springs jump to their target. | All spring physics |\n54\t| L4 Wrapper branches | Wrappers branch on `reduced` to drop parallax and scroll-linked transforms, stop loops and autoplay (text loop, infinite slider), disable fling, and swap transforms for short fades or nothing. | What L2 and L3 do not cover |\n55\t| L5 Non-motion feedback | Pressed, focus and selected states read without motion, through color, outline or shape. | Reduced-motion users still get feedback |\n56\t| L6 Visible toggle | Optional \"Reduce motion\" control persisted to localStorage and fed into `useMotionPreference`. Open decision, not committed. | Users whose OS setting is off but who want calm |\n57\t\n58\t## Ownership matrix\n59\t\n60\tMOT-02. Every interaction class has exactly one owner.\n61\t\n62\t| Interaction class | Owner | Why |\n63\t|-------------------|-------|-----|\n64\t| Mount, unmount and presence | motion (`AnimatePresence`) | Mature exit handling under React 19 |\n65\t| Layout and shared-element morphs | motion (`layout`, `layoutId`) | react-spring has no equivalent |\n66\t| Scroll-linked values and in-view reveals | motion (`useScroll`, `whileInView`) | Already bundled |\n67\t| Text and number effects, motion-primitives prefabs | motion | The primitives are written against it |\n68\t| Velocity physics, press-squish, rail lift with neighbor shift, theme toggle thumb | react-spring (`useSpring`, `useSprings`) | Continuous retargeting gives the tactile signature |\n69\t| Color and hover transitions, native scroll-snap rail | CSS | Zero JS cost |\n70\t| Desktop wheel smoothing | Lenis | Wheel only, off on touch |\n71\t\n72\tConstraints:\n73\t\n74\t- Install `@react-spring/web` at `~10.1.x` only; never the umbrella `react-spring` package.\n75\t- Avoid `useTransition` in core UI; presence is motion's job, which keeps the react-spring v11 migration trivial.\n76\t- `@use-gesture/react` is not added up front.\n77\t- Import motion only from `motion/react`, never raw `framer-motion`.\n78\t- Whether react-spring stays at all is decided after the rail is measured (bundle cost and feel).\n79\t\n80\t## Vendored motion-primitives\n81\t\n82\tCopied in as owned source under `src/components/motion-primitives/`, not installed from npm.\n83\t\n84\t| Component | Used for | Notes |\n85\t|-----------|----------|-------|\n86\t| TextEffect or TextLoop | IX-01 | Role line only |\n87\t| MorphingDialog | IX-05 | Adoption is subject to the overlay accessibility ADR and its spike |\n88\t| AnimatedNumber with InView | IX-12 | Once |\n89\t| InfiniteSlider | IX-13 | not vendored (IX-13 dropped) |\n90\t| Tilt, Magnetic, Spotlight | IX-17 | Fine pointer only |\n91\t\n92\tNot vendored: Cursor, Dock and any other mouse-only primitive. Each vendored file is patched for type-only imports and gets a reduced-motion branch.\n93\t\n94\t## Interaction catalog index\n95\t\n96\tIX-01 to IX-17 are fixed. 4\n137\t\n138\t### IX-02 Press-squish on buttons and cards\n139\t\n140\t- Section: global\n141\t- Trigger: pointerdown and pointerup on buttons and cards, and Enter or Space keydown and keyup on Plan 01-05 completed it: principles, tokens, reduced-motion layers, ownership matrix, vendored primitives, the other 16 interaction specs and the element ownership check.\n\n## Ownership rule\n\n- Exactly one library animates any element: motion, react-spring, CSS or Lenis. Never two on the same element or property.\n- No Tailwind transition utilities on an element a library animates.\n- react-spring is scoped to IX-02, IX-03, IX-06 and IX-10 (velocity-carrying, tactile physics). Everything else uses motion, CSS or Lenis as the catalog says.\n\n## Principles\n\n- Motion never gates content. Name, role and CTAs are visible at first paint. The hero text effect runs only on the role line and never delays it.\n- Animate transform and opacity only, plus motion layout animations where an interaction needs them (IX-05, IX-07, IX-08, IX-11, IX-14).\n- Fine-pointer effects are gated by the media query `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and carry no hover-only content (MOT-04). Touch gets a tap or press equivalent, or nothing.\n- `touch-action` is set only on small draggables. The project rail uses native horizontal scrolling, so vertical page scroll is never captured.\n- Infinite or looping motion pauses when off-screen or when the tab is hidden.\n- Motion budget: entrance animations take at most 420 ms; stagger is at most 60 ms per item for at most 6 items; nothing blocks input.\n\n## Motion tokens\n\nCanonical home is `src/anim/tokens.ts`, with CSS mirrors `--dur-fast`, `--dur-base`, `--dur-slow` and `--ease-out`. One table drives both libraries so they feel like one system.\n\n| Token | Kind | motion format (stiffness, damping, mass) | react-spring format (tension, friction, mass) | Value |\n|-------|------|------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|\n| snappy | spring | 500, 32, 1 | 500, 32, 1 | presses, toggles |\n| gentle | spring | 170, 26, 1 | 170, 26, 1 | rail lift, layout settling |\n| bouncy | spring | 300, 14, 1 | 300, 14, 1 | playful overshoot, used sparingly |\n| fast | duration | n/a | n/a | 120 ms |\n| base | duration | n/a | n/a | 220 ms |\n| slow | duration | n/a | n/a | 420 ms |\n| ease-out | easing | n/a | n/a | cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) |\n\nreact-spring `tension` equals motion `stiffness` and `friction` equals `damping`. The spring numbers are starting values, to be tuned on a real iPhone and a real Android phone during the signature-rail work (Phase 4).\n\n## Reduced motion\n\nOne preference source (MOT-01): `useMotionPreference` reads `prefers-reduced-motion` with a `change` listener (users toggle it live) and feeds three consumers:\n\n- motion: `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (from `motion/react`).\n- react-spring: `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` from `@react-spring/web`, set in an effect with a dependency array and a cleanup that resets it.\n- CSS: the guard `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, which also gates smooth scroll behind `no-preference`.\n\nLenis is not started under reduced motion (MOT-05). Motion's `user` mode still animates opacity, so text effects and other opacity-driven wrappers branch manually on the hook's `reduced` value.\n\n| Layer | Mechanism | Covers |\n|-------|-----------|--------|\n| L0 Progressive enhancement | Content is visible by default in HTML and CSS. Reveal wrappers set the hidden initial state only after mount on the client, and `<noscript>` guarantees visibility. | JS failure, slow hydration, crawlers, screenshots |\n| L1 CSS guard | `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` collapses animation and transition durations to near zero, runs animations once and sets `scroll-behavior: auto`. | CSS transitions, keyframes, anchor scroll |\n| L2 motion | `MotionConfig` `reducedMotion` (\"user\", or \"always\" and \"never\" from an override). Disables transform and layout animations, keeps opacity and color. | All motion components, including vendored primitives |\n| L3 react-spring | `Globals.assign({ skipAnimation })` in the provider effect. Springs jump to their target. | All spring physics |\n| L4 Wrapper branches | Wrappers branch on `reduced` to drop parallax and scroll-linked transforms, stop loops and autoplay (text loop, infinite slider), disable fling, and swap transforms for short fades or nothing. | What L2 and L3 do not cover |\n| L5 Non-motion feedback | Pressed, focus and selected states read without motion, through color, outline or shape. | Reduced-motion users still get feedback |\n| L6 Visible toggle | Optional \"Reduce motion\" control persisted to localStorage and fed into `useMotionPreference`. Open decision, not committed. | Users whose OS setting is off but who want calm |\n\n## Ownership matrix\n\nMOT-02. Every interaction class has exactly one owner.\n\n| Interaction class | Owner | Why |\n|-------------------|-------|-----|\n| Mount, unmount and presence | motion (`AnimatePresence`) | Mature exit handling under React 19 |\n| Layout and shared-element morphs | motion (`layout`, `layoutId`) | react-spring has no equivalent |\n| Scroll-linked values and in-view reveals | motion (`useScroll`, `whileInView`) | Already bundled |\n| Text and number effects, motion-primitives prefabs | motion | The primitives are written against it |\n| Velocity physics, press-squish, rail lift with neighbor shift, theme toggle thumb | react-spring (`useSpring`, `useSprings`) | Continuous retargeting gives the tactile signature |\n| Color and hover transitions, native scroll-snap rail | CSS | Zero JS cost |\n| Desktop wheel smoothing | Lenis | Wheel only, off on touch |\n\nConstraints:\n\n- Install `@react-spring/web` at `~10.1.x` only; never the umbrella `react-spring` package.\n- Avoid `useTransition` in core UI; presence is motion's job, which keeps the react-spring v11 migration trivial.\n- `@use-gesture/react` is not added up front.\n- Import motion only from `motion/react`, never raw `framer-motion`.\n- Whether react-spring stays at all is decided after the rail is measured (bundle cost and feel).\n\n## Vendored motion-primitives\n\nCopied in as owned source under `src/components/motion-primitives/`, not installed from npm.\n\n| Component | Used for | Notes |\n|-----------|----------|-------|\n| TextEffect or TextLoop | IX-01 | Role line only |\n| MorphingDialog | IX-05 | Adoption is subject to the overlay accessibility ADR and its spike |\n| AnimatedNumber with InView | IX-12 | Once |\n| InfiniteSlider | IX-13 | not vendored (IX-13 dropped) |\n| Tilt, Magnetic, Spotlight | IX-17 | Fine pointer only |\n\nNot vendored: Cursor, Dock and any other mouse-only primitive. Each vendored file is patched for type-only imports and gets a reduced-motion branch.\n\n## Interaction catalog index\n\nIX-01 to IX-17 are fixed. IX-18 was added by the Phase 3 art direction. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GFQ6rHbXLJrEKu8w6aQ3jd","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ADR-0003: GitHub Pages source, staging, cutover and rollback\n2\t\n3\tStatus: Accepted\n4\t\n5\tDate: 2026-10-09\n6\t\n7\t## Context\n8\t\n9\tThe current iPod site is served from the `aa-phan.github.io` repository by the legacy \"Deploy from a branch\" Pages source. The live setting was read from the GitHub API on 2026-10-09:\n10\t\n11\t```\n12\tgh api repos/aa-phan/aa-phan.github.io/pages --jq '{build_type, source, html_url}'\n13\t{\"build_type\":\"legacy\",\"html_url\":\"https://aa-phan.github.io/\",\"source\":{\"branch\":\"main\",\"path\":\"/\"}}\n14\t```\n15\t\n16\tSo the live site is published from branch `main`, path `/`, with `build_type` `legacy`. A Vite build cannot be served that way: the new site needs the \"GitHub Actions\" source, which changes how the live URL is published.\n17\t\n18\tThis development repository is not yet on GitHub. The OD-01 gate on pushing it is resolved (see the [ADR log](README.md)).\n19\t\n20\t## Decision\n21\t\n22\t1. The new site is built by GitHub Actions and first deployed as a staging project site of this repository. `VITE_BASE` is set to `/` plus this repository's name plus `/`, so the staging URL is `https://aa-phan.github.io/aa-phan-portfolio-v2/` and CI catches broken sub-path assets before launch.\n23\t2. The cutover is an additive commit on top of the existing `aa-phan.github.io` history. First the iPod site is tagged (`v1-ipod`) and that tag and a matching branch are pushed, so the old site stays recoverable. Then the iPod files are removed and the new site source is added in a normal commit, merged through a pull request.\n24\t3. The Pages source of `aa-phan.github.io` is switched from the legacy branch source to GitHub Actions in the same sitting as the merge, and the deploy workflow is then triggered with `workflow_dispatch` so the new site goes live immediately.\n25\t4. As a modal dialog it must:\n10\t\n11\t1. Trap keyboard focus inside the overlay while it is open.\n12\t2. Close on Escape.\n13\t3. Lock background scroll.\n14\t4. The two concerns stay separate.\n26\t\n27\tA code spike checks `MorphingDialog` against the seven-point checklist before the rail ships. The spike itself is deferred to the interaction build (Phase 2 or 4) and is not run as part of the documentation work.\n28\t\n29\t- If every point passes, `MorphingDialog` is used as vendored.\n30\t- If any point fails, the overlay uses a native `dialog` element opened with `showModal()`. Top-layer rendering makes the rest of the page inert and the `cancel` event handles Escape. Focus return and scroll lock are handled explicitly in our code. Motion animates only the inner panel; the `layoutId` morph targets that inner panel rendered inside the `dialog` element, not the `dialog` element itself.\n31\t- Radix Dialog is considered only if both of the above fail, because it adds a dependency.\n32\t\n33\t## Consequences\n34\t\n35\t- Overlay animation and overlay accessibility are separate concerns, so either primitive works with the same motion spec and the same reduced-motion fallback (instant open and close, no morph).\n36\t- The native fallback costs a little explicit code (focus return, scroll lock) and no new dependency.\n37\t- With the native fallback, the backdrop blur and the morph are applied to elements inside the `dialog`, because the `dialog` element's own box is not what animates.\n38\t- The rail cannot ship until the spike result is recorded.\n39\t\n40\t## Alternatives considered\n41\t\n42\t- Adopt `MorphingDialog` without checking it. Rejected: an unverified focus trap and Escape path is an accessibility failure on the site's main interaction.\n43\t- Always use the native `dialog` element. Not chosen as the default only because `MorphingDialog` may already pass and would then be less code; it stays the fallback.\n44\t- Radix Dialog. Held back: it solves the checklist but adds a dependency for one overlay.\n45\t- Build a custom focus trap. Expose `role=\"dialog\"` with `aria-modal=\"true\"` and a label taken from the project title.\n7. Keep previous, next and close reachable and usable by keyboard.\n\nThe vendored `MorphingDialog` component from motion-primitives gives the morph animation. Its behavior on the seven points above has not been verified.\n\nThe motion spec splits responsibility the same way: motion animates the overlay, and the dialog primitive owns focus, Escape, inert background and scroll lock.\n\n## Decision\n\nMotion owns the overlay animation: `AnimatePresence` plus a shared `layoutId` morph from the rail item's inner card to the overlay panel, with a crossfade for previous and next. The dialog primitive owns everything on the checklist above: focus trap, Escape, inert background, scroll lock and focus return. The two concerns stay separate.\n\nA code spike checks `MorphingDialog` against the seven-point checklist before the rail ships. The spike itself is deferred to the interaction build (Phase 2 or 4) and is not run as part of the documentation work.\n\n- If every point passes, `MorphingDialog` is used as vendored.\n- If any point fails, the overlay uses a native `dialog` element opened with `showModal()`. Top-layer rendering makes the rest of the page inert and the `cancel` event handles Escape. Focus return and scroll lock are handled explicitly in our code. Motion animates only the inner panel; the `layoutId` morph targets that inner panel rendered inside the `dialog` element, not the `dialog` element itself.\n- Radix Dialog is considered only if both of the above fail, because it adds a dependency.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Overlay animation and overlay accessibility are separate concerns, so either primitive works with the same motion spec and the same reduced-motion fallback (instant open and close, no morph).\n- The native fallback costs a little explicit code (focus return, scroll lock) and no new dependency.\n- With the native fallback, the backdrop blur and the morph are applied to elements inside the `dialog`, because the `dialog` element's own box is not what animates.\n- The rail cannot ship until the spike result is recorded.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- Adopt `MorphingDialog` without checking it. Rejected: an unverified focus trap and Escape path is an accessibility failure on the site's main interaction.\n- Always use the native `dialog` element. Not chosen as the default only because `MorphingDialog` may already pass and would then be less code; it stays the fallback.\n- Radix Dialog. Held back: it solves the checklist but adds a dependency for one overlay.\n- Build a custom focus trap. Rejected: the native `dialog` element already provides one.\n\n## Revisit when\n\nThe spike result is recorded (open decision OD-06), or if the overlay design changes so it is no longer modal.\n","numLines":50,"startLine":1,"totalLines":50}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01NdQd4BhF5M1dTRTFBT2Hq4","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
